approved_forms: niacin (nicotinic acid, CHEMBL573, max_phase 4) and niacinamide/nicotinamide (CHEMBL1140, max_phase 4). Nicotinamide riboside (CHEMBL438497, max_phase 3) and nicotinamide mononucleotide are NOT approved drugs - adjunct consideration only per plan section 0.

approval.note: NIACOR (nicotinic acid) label queried; approved for hypercholesterolemia adjunct therapy. NAD-restoration use is off-label.

claims.text: Axis-A anchor: the age-related decline of BubR1 protein is driven by declining NAD+ and loss of SIRT2-mediated deacetylation of BubR1 lysine-668 (opposed by CBP acetylation); in mice, SIRT2 overexpression OR treatment with the NAD+ precursor NMN increased BubR1 abundance in vivo, and SIRT2 overexpression extended median lifespan specifically in BubR1-hypomorphic (H/H) animals.

Raising BubR1 abundance is itself disease-modifying in models: sustained high BubR1 expression in mice preserves genomic integrity, corrects checkpoint and microtubule-kinetochore attachment defects, reduces tumorigenesis even with oncogenic Ras, and extends healthy lifespan - the proof that increasing residual BubR1 output compensates a defective checkpoint.

Independent lab confirmation with honest bound: SIRT2 overexpression rescues health and lifespan in the BubR1-hypomorph model via improved BubR1 protein stability, but the same overexpression in wild-type mice had NO effect on health or lifespan - i.e. the SIRT2 benefit appears conditional on BubR1 under-expression, which is exactly the MVA1 situation (null + hypomorph alleles) but offers no general-longevity claim.

Class-level clinical plausibility: NAD+ supplementation shows benefit in several premature-ageing and DNA-repair-deficiency diseases where PARP hyperactivation depletes NAD+, with a favourable safety profile - a review-level support for NAD restoration in rare progeroid/genome-instability disease, though MVA itself was not studied.

Critical pharmacology caveat: nicotinamide is BOTH an NAD+ precursor AND an end-product inhibitor of sirtuin deacetylases (established for yeast Sir2 and human SIRT1) - so high-dose nicotinamide could theoretically inhibit the very SIRT2-BubR1 axis it is meant to fuel. Nicotinic acid (niacin) raises NAD+ via the Preiss-Handler pathway without product inhibition of sirtuins; the choice of form is therefore mechanistically non-trivial.

Mechanistic nuance: SIRT2 also deacetylates BubR1 at K250 during prometaphase, where deacetylation promotes timely APC/C-mediated BubR1 degradation at mitotic exit; SIRT2 regulation of BubR1 is site- and context-specific, so 'more SIRT2 activity' does not linearly equal 'more BubR1'.

pediatric.label_source: openFDA drug/label set_id bf287412-160b-403f-8eb4-57f29a475902 (effective 2021-12-23); NIACOR (nicotinic acid)
pediatric.approved_pediatric_indication: None. Label states verbatim: 'Pediatric Use - Safety and effectiveness in children and adolescents have not been established.' (quoted label fact)
key_risks: Niacin at lipid-lowering doses: flushing, hepatotoxicity (label contraindicates significant/unexplained hepatic dysfunction), hyperglycaemia, hyperuricaemia, GI/peptic-ulcer caution - the approved-dose adverse profile is adult-derived.
Nutritional-dose nicotinamide/niacin (vitamin-level) has a wide safety margin in children, but the NAD-restoration hypothesis may require pharmacologic doses - an open question.
Form-choice risk (claim c5): pharmacologic nicotinamide could inhibit sirtuins; the safe-form question is unresolved, not a detail.
No reproductive-age considerations for the child directly; family context includes recurrent spontaneous abortion - niacin pregnancy safety is not established at pharmacologic doses.
monitoring: If used in the supplements research program: BubR1 protein and NAD+ levels as pharmacodynamic markers

celegans.assay: san-1 mutant + NAD+ precursor exposure (sir-2.1 is the worm SIRT1/2-family deacetylase)
celegans.readout: embryonic viability, him rate, growth, lifespan
celegans.expected: rescue direction if NAD/SIRT axis stabilises residual SAN-1 function; clean genetic test

fibroblasts.assay: NAD+ precursor exposure on MVA patient fibroblasts
fibroblasts.readout: BubR1 protein level (western/IF), NAD+ level, aneuploidy rate, mitotic timing under nocodazole
fibroblasts.expected: increased BubR1 abundance = the direct Axis-A pharmacodynamic readout; then whether aneuploidy rate falls

supplements.assay: directly aligned - the society's supplements program tests supplement-driven stabilisation of MVA cells
supplements.expected: NR/NMN would likely be tested here as supplements while niacin/nicotinamide are the approved-drug forms

verdict_reason: The only Axis-A candidate: rather than managing downstream damage, it aims to raise abundance of the residual hypomorphic BubR1 allele's output - the most disease-modifying mechanism available, anchored by the EMBO J 2014 result that NAD+/SIRT2 raises BubR1 in vivo and extends BubR1-hypomorph lifespan (PMID:24825348), independently replicated as BubR1-conditional (PMID:38009412), and matched to the MVA Society's supplements program direction. Approved forms exist (niacin CHEMBL573, niacinamide CHEMBL1140, both phase 4). Rank tempered by the nicotinamide-sirtuin-inhibition paradox (PMID:12297502), absence of pediatric approval, and the fact that NMN - the exact molecule used in the anchor study - is a supplement, so the approved-form evidence is extrapolated.
